ambiguities.description: Optionality of enrollment and grading: The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in,' but does not clarify whether every enrolled student must receive a grade, or whether a student can be enrolled without a grade (e.g., if they drop or receive an incomplete). Are there enrollment records without grades, and should the grade-receiving relationship be mandatory?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. The grade is one of A, B, C, D, or F. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Identification of enrollment: The objectified fact type 'Student enrolls in CourseOffering' (i.e., Enrollment) currently has no explicit reference mode. Should Enrollment have its own identifier (e.g., an enrollment_id), or is it identified by the combination of Student and CourseOffering? This affects whether Enrollment is truly a primary entity or merely a junction table.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Capacity constraint enforcement: The transcript mentions that each offering has a maximum capacity, but does not specify any business rule about what happens when enrollment reaches capacity or how the constraint is enforced (e.g., is it a hard limit, or can overrides occur?). Should a frequency or exclusion constraint be applied?

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

ambiguities.description: Historical tracking of enrollment and grades: The transcript describes 'at the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade,' which implies grades are recorded after a semester completes. Should the model track when grades are recorded, or whether historical grades (from previous enrollments) are archived? Is the enrollment-grade relationship current-state only, or should temporal dimensions be included?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: One-to-many cardinality clarity: The transcript states 'an instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester,' which confirms the offering-to-instructor direction is many-to-one. However, it does not explicitly state whether an instructor must teach at least one offering, or whether instructors without assigned offerings should exist in the system. Should a mandatory constraint be applied to the 'teaches' role?
